note:
## What this paper is

2019 ICM D, team 1922748: "A Systematic Dynamic Route Planning Model". An N&M/SES microscopic
speed model feeds a node graph and a matrix model of the venue, a Ford-Fulkerson-based dynamic
system planning algorithm solves it, and the whole thing is validated on a six-room
hypothetical building and then run on the five floors of the Louvre. A 30-page file, 17 of
whose pages carry art, 42 measured regions - **all 42 are exhibits**: 18 printed figures
(15 numbered + 3 lettered appendix ones) and 2 tables, giving 40 figure rows and 2 table rows.
No refusals, no deficits. Every figure row is a RASTER paste; the only vector art in the file
is the two tables (21 and 14 paths).

## Which section takes which exhibit

- 1.3 "Overview of our work" takes the two orientation exhibits: **Figure 1** (the mind map)
  whose pointer is the last line of 1.2, and **Figure 2** (the method flow chart).
- Section 3 takes **Table 1**, the symbol table - the paper's only symbol table.
- 4.2 takes **Table 2** (the speed coefficient k, two header rows), pointed at from 4.1.
- 5.1 takes **Figure 3** (the six-room teaching graph); 5.3.1 takes **Figure 4** (the block
  matrix picture) whose lead sentence is the last line of 5.2.
- 6.1 takes **Figure 5** (model initialization, every weight printed); 6.2 takes **Figure 6**
  (the three-panel flow strip); 6.3.1 takes **Figure 7** (the bottleneck pair) and 6.3.2
  **Figure 8** (remaining people against time); 6.4 takes **Figure 9** (the four-state
  adaptive strip).
- 7.1 takes **Figures 10 and 11** (the real 1F plan beside its node graph, then the five
  stacked floors); 7.2.1 takes **Figure 12** (the four-stage flow strip); 7.2.2 takes
  **Figures 13 and 14** (the export flow curve, then the margin strip).
- 9.1 takes **Figure 15** (the sensitivity pair).
- The appendix's "Other figures" page carries **Figures A-1, A-2 and A-3** - the algorithm
  flow chart and the ten real/simulation floor pairs.

So the shape is: one drawing per question in the model half, and then the result half gives
every finding a (curve, node graph) pair, with the algorithm chart demoted to the appendix.

## When it goes 3-D

For the Louvre only, and only one way. **Figures 11, 12(a-d) and 14(a-d)** - nine rows out of
forty - are the same five floor plates (2F, 1F, 0F, -1F, -2F) drawn as stacked parallelograms
in an oblique projection, joined by vertical stair edges. The projection is used for one
reason: it is the only way to show inter-floor edges without drawing five separate graphs.
Everything else - the six-room model, the four chart figures, the appendix pairs - is flat,
and the paper never uses a colourbar, a surface mesh or a photograph.

## What the tables do that the figures cannot

The two tables carry constants, not results: Table 1 defines the symbols, Table 2 gives the
speed coefficient k by channel type. Neither is a data table and neither is ever read back -
no prose sentence quotes a cell. Every number the paper argues about lives in a figure's axis
or edge label instead.

Table shapes worth reusing:

| table | shape | trick |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Table 1 symbols | 3 cols, 9 rows, thin horizontals + full-height verticals | units are their own column, '\\' marks the dimensionless ones |
| Table 2 speed coefficient | 4 cols, 7 rows, two header rows | the bottom row merges three cells to say 'this row is one channel type' |

## Caption template

`Figure N:` with a **COLON on 18 of 18** figures, and `Figure A-N:` with the same colon for the
three appendix ones (Tables use `Table N:` too - this paper has no period captions at all).
Then a bare noun phrase of 4-8 words: "Problem unfolding", "Method and process", "Node graph
of a hypothetical building", "Louvre's spatial node graph". No unit, no variable, no
condition, no finding. Captions sit BELOW the art on 37 of 40 rows; the three that sit above
are the ones at the head of a page (Figure 1, Figure 11, A-1).

## Context connectives

- **"as shown in Figure N"**: 17 of 30 pointed rows. The paper's default, and it survives a
  misspelling of the number itself: "which is shown in Figure9 (c), (d)" - no space.
- **"Figure N shows ..."**: 6 rows, always the naming first: "Figure 10 shows the results of
  first floor (1F)[23] as an example."
- **direct**: 5 rows, a bare statement with the number in the middle: "It can be seen from
  Figure 13, the personnel in the hall can basically be evacuated within five minutes."
- **parenthetical**: 2 rows, and both are the earliest exhibits: "The mind map (Figure 1)
  shows the issues that need to be addressed."
- **never named**: 10 rows - every appendix panel except A-1, plus Table 1 - carried by the
  heading alone.
- Read-backs always quantify: "the absolute values of the slopes of nodes 3 and 2 are smaller
  than those of nodes 4 and 5", "the four green lines meet at a point, which is the sink
  point", "a channel is fully loaded".

## Layer defects found in the measured layout

- **Section paths weld FORWARD**: six rows re-assigned from the prose (Figure 1 from 1.2 to
  1.3, Table 2 from 4.1 to 4.2, Figure 4 from 5.2 to 5.3.1, Figure 6 from 6.2 to 6.3.1,
  Figure 11 from 7.1 to 7.2.1, Figure 14 from 7.2.2 to 9.1).
- **The caption detector double-hits Figure 14**: on p19 the body sentence "Figure 14 shows a
  schematic diagram of the margin of channel flow at each time." is counted as a caption in
  addition to the real one under the art on p20.
- **Figure 12 is pointed at from the page AFTER it**: the exhibit is on p18, its first prose
  pointer on p19, so the row records a negative page gap (-1).
- **Printed panels are not in reading order**: on p16 the letters run (a),(b) over (d),(c)
  left-to-right per region index, i.e. the art's own order is column-major while the captions
  are row-major; the same on p18 for Figure 12 (c)/(d) and p26/p27 for the appendix pairs.
- **p28-p30 carry 21 vector paths that are not an exhibit**: they are code typography
  (underscores, brackets, broken-space glyphs) in the appendix's MATLAB listing, which is
  why they are outside the measured region set.
- **The folio stops before the appendix**: "page N of 20" prints on p3-p22 only, and the file
  is 30 pages, so the appendix pages carry no page number at all.

## Declared deficits

None. All 42 measured regions are exhibit panels or tables, and every printed exhibit in the
file has a region.

The exhibit vocabulary is a small kit reused to exhaustion: 25 node graphs, 6 line charts, 6 floor plans and 3 schematics cover 40 rows, and the same nine-node graph is redrawn for Figures 3, 5, 6 and 9 with only the edge weights changed. [geometry.family]

A figure is redrawn rather than recomposed when only the numbers change: Figure 6's three panels and Figure 12's four panels are the identical topology at successive times, so the reader compares numbers in the same positions instead of comparing layouts. [geometry.panel_count]

Thirty-four of forty rows carry NO legend; the six that do are the line charts plus Figure 3. Everything else encodes with colour and explains it in the prose - the three matrices of Figure 5 ('red = remaining, olive = capacity, grey-blue = exit flow') and the red/blue loading of Figure 14 are keyed by sentence, never by a key box. [geometry.legend]

The one legend pushed outside the art is on the teaching graph (Figure 3, outside-right), which is also the only figure whose markers are explained at all (stairs dash-dot, corridor solid, room dot). [geometry.legend]

Captions are a COLON and nothing else: 18 of 18 figures print 'Figure N:' and both tables print 'Table N:' - the paper never uses the period form, and the appendix keeps the same colon with a lettered number ('Figure A-1:'). [caption.numbering]

Captions run 4-8 words and are bare noun phrases: 'Problem unfolding', 'Model initialization', 'Export flow-time diagram'. Not one carries a unit, a variable, a condition or a conclusion. [caption.words]

Captions sit BELOW the art on 37 of 40 rows; the three above are exactly the exhibits printed at the head of a page (Figure 1, Figure 11, A-1), i.e. position follows the page break rather than the exhibit type. [caption.position]

Panel letters are printed under each panel and the caption ONCE under the whole strip, and the strip always varies one thing: time in Figures 6, 12 and 14, normal against emergency in Figure 9, real against simulation in the appendix pairs. [geometry.panel_layout]

'as shown in Figure N' is the default pointer on 17 of 30 pointed rows, and it survives even a typo in the label itself ('shown in Figure9 (c), (d)' - no space before the digit). [mention.lead_pattern]

The exhibit number is placed FIRST in the sentence when the prose wants to name the object ('Figure 10 shows the results of first floor (1F)[23] as an example') and MID-SENTENCE when it wants to report a reading ('It can be seen from Figure 13, ...') - six rows and five rows respectively. [mention.style]
Ten rows are never named in prose at all, and they are the appendix: every A-2 and A-3 panel, and Table 1. The appendix is navigated by its heading, not by reference. [mention.first_page]

The one exhibit pointed at from a later page is Figure 12: the art is on p18 and the first sentence that names it is on p19, a page gap of -1, because the strip is introduced as a whole and then read panel by panel on the next page. [mention.lead_pages]

Read-backs report a SHAPE, not a value: 'the absolute values of the slopes of nodes 3 and 2 are smaller than those of nodes 4 and 5', 'the four green lines meet at a point, which is the sink point'. The one number quoted in a read-back is a time ('within five minutes'). [mention.trail_sentence]

Numbers are written into the drawing only where the drawing IS the data: 21 of 40 rows print numerals (node IDs and edge weights), while no line chart carries a single data label - the six line rows are read off the axes. [geometry.printed_numbers]

The twelve rows with data labels are all node graphs, labelled with node IDs and weights at the same size as the axis text; the appendix's simulation panels drop the weights, so a panel that only claims topology prints less rather than more. [geometry.data_labels]

The algorithm chart the body leans on hardest is the one exhibit sent to the appendix: section 5.3.2 names Figure A-1 twice and hands the reader a page 13 pages away, which is the cheapest way to keep a long chart out of the argument. [place.section_path]

Table 1 mixes two rule systems: booktabs-thin horizontals (above the header, under it and at the foot) with full-height verticals on every column boundary including the outer two, so its grid reads heavier than Table 2's boxed grid despite carrying less information. [table.rule_style]

Table 2 is the only table that needs two header rows and a merged row: 'Evacuation Channel Type' spans three columns, 'k' sits over the fourth, the stair cases work as a vertical stub under 'Stairs', and the last row merges three cells into one 'Corridor,Aisle,Ramp,Doorway' with a single k. The merge IS the statement. [table.merged_cells]

Both tables put units where they belong structurally: a units column of its own in Table 1 (with '\\' standing for dimensionless) and 'Riser/mm', 'Tread/mm' inside Table 2's header. No table in the paper has a note row except Table 1, which prints one as a body sentence under the grid. [table.units_in_header]

Model exhibits and result exhibits are kept in different sections: every schematic and every table lives in sections 1-5 (plus 6.1-6.2), every result chart and every Louvre drawing in 6.3-9.1, and the appendix holds only the two things too long or too numerous for the body. [place.section_kind]

tables.note: The symbol table: 'symbol | descriptions | units', eight rows from v to G. Rules are vertical on every column boundary including the outer two, with horizontals only above the header, under it and at the foot - a grid whose horizontals are booktabs-thin while its verticals are full height, which is why the two grids of this paper do not look alike. Units are a column of their own and three symbols carry '\' instead (D, k, G are dimensionless). One note row, printed in the body not in the grid.

table.note_sentence: Note: Symbols not mentioned in the table will be explained if they appear below.

mention.lead_sentence: And k in the formula (1) can be determined from Table 2[5].

tables.note: Two header rows: 'Evacuation Channel Type' spans the first three columns and 'k' sits alone over the fourth; below it 'Stairs' is a vertical stub over the four stair cases while 'Riser/mm' and 'Tread/mm' name the two measured columns. The bottom row merges all three left-hand cells into one ('Corridor,Aisle,Ramp, Doorway') and prints a single k of 1.40, so the merge itself says 'this row is a different channel type', and the two stair constants the paper then uses (1.00, 1.40) are the first and last rows.
